content.overview: Every company other than a One Person Company must hold an AGM each year. The first AGM must be held within nine months of the close of the first financial year; later AGMs must be held within six months of the close of each financial year, with no more than fifteen months between AGMs. If the first AGM is held within that period, no AGM is required in the year of incorporation. For special reasons, the Registrar may extend the time for an AGM other than the first by no more than three months.

content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 96 (Annual general meeting). Every company other than a One Person Company must hold an AGM each year. The first AGM must be held within nine months from the close of the first financial year; each subsequent AGM must be held within six months from the close of the financial year, and the gap between two AGMs must not exceed fifteen months. If the first AGM is held within that period, the company need not hold an AGM in the year of its incorporation. For special reasons, the Registrar may extend the time for holding an AGM other than the first AGM by no more than three months. The AGM must be held during business hours (9 a.m. to 6 p.m.) on a day that is not a National Holiday, at the registered office or another place within the city, town or village where the registered office is situated. An unlisted company may hold the AGM at any place in India if all Members give advance consent in writing or electronically; the Central Government may exempt a company from the place/time subsection subject to conditions. Ordinary business includes consideration of financial statements and reports, declaration of dividend, appointment of directors in place of those retiring, and appointment/remuneration of auditors. Default may engage section 99 and Tribunal relief under section 97. The topic remains under source and current-law review.

sections.heading: Annual timing
sections.body: Every company other than a One Person Company must hold an AGM each year. The first AGM is due within nine months after close of the first financial year; subsequent AGMs are due within six months after close of the financial year; no more than fifteen months may elapse between AGMs. If the first AGM is held within that period, no AGM is required in the year of incorporation.

sections.heading: Registrar extension
sections.body: For special reasons, the Registrar may extend the time for holding an AGM other than the first AGM by a period not exceeding three months.

sections.heading: Time and place
sections.body: An AGM must be held during business hours, between 9 a.m. and 6 p.m., on a day that is not a National Holiday, at the registered office or another place within the city, town or village in which the registered office is situated. A National Holiday includes a day declared as such by the Central Government.

sections.heading: Unlisted-company place exception and exemption
sections.body: An unlisted company may hold an AGM at any place in India if all Members give consent in writing or by electronic mode in advance. The Central Government may exempt any company from the time/place requirements in subsection (2), subject to conditions it imposes.

sections.heading: Ordinary business and default
sections.body: Ordinary business includes consideration of financial statements and reports of the Board and auditors, declaration of dividend, appointment of directors in place of those retiring, and appointment/remuneration of auditors. A default in holding an AGM may engage section 99 and an application to the Tribunal under section 97.

hypotheticals.question: A company held its first AGM within nine months after the close of its first financial year. Must it also hold an AGM in the year of incorporation?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 96 states that where the first AGM is held within the specified period, the company need not hold an AGM in the year of its incorporation. Check the actual close date and AGM date.

hypotheticals.question: An unlisted company wants to hold its AGM outside the city, town or village of its registered office. What condition must it check?
hypotheticals.analysis: The section permits an unlisted company to hold the AGM at any place in India if all Members give consent in writing or electronically in advance. Check the advance consent and whether any applicable exemption or condition applies.

distinctions.title: AGM timing and Tribunal remedies
distinctions.left: Section 96 imposes the annual-meeting duty, timing limits and place/time rules.
distinctions.right: Section 97 provides a Tribunal route when the company defaults in holding an AGM; section 99 states the penalty for specified defaults.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming the Registrar may extend the time for the first AGM.
misconceptions.correction: The extension power is for an AGM other than the first AGM and cannot exceed three months.

misconceptions.trap: Ignoring the fifteen-month maximum interval or the first-AGM incorporation-year rule.
misconceptions.correction: Apply both the timing limits and the specific rule for the year of incorporation.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming any company may hold an AGM anywhere in India without consent.
misconceptions.correction: The special any-place-in-India exception applies to an unlisted company with advance written/electronic consent of all Members.

misconceptions.trap: Importing unrelated corporate judgments or evidence-law material into the AGM timing rule.
misconceptions.correction: Keep this topic focused on section 96, the applicable rules and relevant cross-references such as sections 97 and 99.
